residence.headline: A modern home, on a quiet street.
residence.body: Recovery doesn't happen in a facility. It happens in a kitchen, a porch, a single bedroom that feels like yours. Step by Step is a private modern residence in a residential St. Louis neighborhood — not an institution dressed up as one. Eight bedrooms, communal living, designed interiors, a kitchen that gets used.
bullets: Eight private bedrooms with hotel-quality linens
Communal kitchen, dining, and living spaces designed for use, not display
Outdoor space — a real porch, a real yard
Walking distance to coffee, transit, and the rhythms of normal life

method.headline: Five things I get right.
method.body: After fifteen years inside this work, I've learned that recovery housing fails for predictable reasons — too many residents, too little structure, no follow-through, no design, no story for what comes next. Step by Step is built around five non-negotiables.

pillars.name: Small by design
pillars.body: Eight residents. Not twelve, not twenty. Every name is known. Every relapse risk is seen early.

pillars.name: Real structure
pillars.body: House meetings, recovery accountability, weekly one-on-ones, sponsor and step-work expectations — written down, followed through.

pillars.name: Dignified setting
pillars.body: A designed home, not a converted facility. The space communicates: you are worth this.

pillars.name: Founder-present
pillars.body: I am in the house every week. Residents know me. Families know how to reach me.

pillars.name: A plan for after
pillars.body: We map the 6-month off-ramp from day one — work, education, sponsorship, housing, family. Discharge isn't a goodbye, it's a handoff.

founder.headline: Why I built Step by Step.
founder.body: I'm Yomi Martin. I founded Step by Step because the city I love — St. Louis — has good treatment, hard-working nonprofits, and a real gap between detox and a sustainable life. The months after treatment are the months that make or break recovery, and the housing options for that window are largely either institutional, under-resourced, or both. I wanted to build the residence I wished existed: small, structured, designed, founder-present, with a plan for what comes after.

why.headline: What "boutique" actually means here.
why.body: Boutique is overused in this industry. Here is what it means at Step by Step:

items.title: Eight residents, never more.
items.body: Capacity is a design choice, not a financial accident. We won't grow this house. We will open another.

items.title: Founder-present, not founder-named.
items.body: I am here. Weekly one-on-ones. Family calls returned the same day. The brand isn't a holding company — it is me, in the house, by name.

items.title: Designed for life, not for liability.
items.body: The home is furnished and finished as a residence, not as a facility. The communal kitchen has good knives. The porch has chairs that hold up to use.

items.title: A plan for after, from day one.
items.body: Recovery isn't a 90-day program. It's a 5-year arc. We map yours — work, school, sponsorship, family — from the first week.

items.title: Family is the second client.
items.body: We assume families are involved unless residents instruct otherwise. Communication is structured, weekly, and not gossip.

investment_teaser.headline: Building the next ten residences.
investment_teaser.body: Step by Step is the first of a planned residence portfolio. If you're an investor, family office, or strategic partner interested in private-pay recovery housing in the Midwest, we have a room for that conversation.

inquiry.headline: I read every inquiry personally.
inquiry.body: Whether you're considering Step by Step for yourself, for a family member, or as a referring professional, I'd like to hear from you. Inquiry is private. Nothing is shared until you choose.

footer_cta.headline: When you're ready, the door is open.

the_residence_page.meta_title: The Residence | Step by Step Recovery St. Louis
the_residence_page.meta_description: Walk through Step by Step's modern St. Louis residence — eight bedrooms, communal living, designed interiors. The home is the program.
the_residence_page.intro: Eight bedrooms. One kitchen that gets used. A porch. A yard. A street with neighbors and trees. Recovery housing that is, at last, just a home.

sections.title: Exterior & neighborhood
sections.body: A modern home in a residential St. Louis neighborhood — tree-lined, walkable, on a real street. We chose the location for the same reason most families would: it feels normal, because it is.

sections.title: Communal interiors
sections.body: Kitchen, dining, living, and library are designed as one connected space — the place where most of recovery actually happens. Good light, good chairs, food made together.

sections.title: Private bedrooms
sections.body: Eight bedrooms, each with its own desk, blackout, and storage. Hotel-quality linens. Locking. Private. Yours.

sections.title: Outdoor space
sections.body: A porch with chairs that hold up to use. A yard for a long phone call. The everyday spaces that make a place feel like a home, not a facility.

partner_page.intro: Step by Step is residence one of a planned portfolio. We are speaking with a small number of investors, family offices, and strategic partners who understand private-pay recovery housing as a category and the Midwest as an underserved market. If that's you, the conversation is private and on your terms.

thesis_blocks.title: The market gap
thesis_blocks.body: St. Louis has nonprofit and insurance-funded recovery housing. It does not have premium private-pay sober living that families with means actually choose. National references — Caron, Hazelden Betty Ford, Mountainside — operate at campus scale; the boutique-residence tier is largely empty in the Midwest.

thesis_blocks.title: The unit economics
thesis_blocks.body: An 8-resident residence at $7,500–$10,500/month, run with operational discipline, is a defensible single-asset business. The portfolio thesis multiplies it across St. Louis, Kansas City, Indianapolis, Louisville, and Memphis.

thesis_blocks.title: The founder
thesis_blocks.body: Yomi Martin has spent fifteen years inside this work. He is the operator, the brand, and the daily presence. Step by Step is not an LP-fronted facility chain; it is a founder-led residence portfolio.

thesis_blocks.title: The structure
thesis_blocks.body: Single-purpose entity per residence. Detailed pro forma, use of funds, and milestones available under NDA. We are not raising on this page — we are inviting a conversation.
